stocks.note: Numbers as of market close on Friday, May 29th.
stocks.news:
Citadel Securities just posted its best quarter ever, pulling in $4.3 billion, up 26% from a year ago as choppy markets kept trading volume high. As a market maker it earns its cut whether stocks rise, fall, or chop sideways, which is a good business to be in right now. Next up it is eyeing crypto, with plans to provide liquidity on exchanges like Coinbase (COIN +3.72%).

Dell (DELL +32.76%) had its best day ever Friday after AI server sales soared 757% to $16.1 billion. Profit landed at $4.86 a share against the $2.94 Wall Street expected, prompting Morgan Stanley to admit it was "eating our humble pie." The AI trade keeps finding new ways to surprise the doubters.

economy.note: US 10-Year and Gold as of 2:20 PM ET, Sunday, May 31st. Brent Crude via Market Briefs.
economy.commentary:
The 10-year Treasury sits at 4.44%, but the forecasts are climbing. Deutsche Bank raised its year-end target to 4.70% from 4.45% and now expects the Fed, under new Chair Kevin Warsh, to stop cutting altogether. "Higher for longer" is moving from a warning to a base case.

Meanwhile the people running companies are getting nervous. CEO confidence fell 12 points last quarter per the Conference Board, and nearly half say the economy is already worse than it was six months ago. The tell, though, is that 37% still plan to spend more on growth, so the wallets are not closing yet. Gold held flat at $4,530.

crypto.note: Numbers as of 6:20 PM ET, Sunday, May 31st.
crypto.commentary:
Bitcoin spot ETFs bled $2.8 billion over nine days, the longest outflow streak since the funds launched in January 2024. The odd part is that stocks hit fresh highs the same week, and crypto usually moves with them, so this divergence is worth watching. Outflows can feed on themselves, with selling pressure dragging prices and lower prices triggering more selling.

On the brighter side, regulators cleared Kalshi to launch Bitcoin perpetual futures, the first U.S.-regulated version of a product that traded over $90 trillion offshore last year. The bets are getting bigger, and now they are legal.

real_estate.homebuilder: Rates Hold At 6.59% For A Third Day As Wall Street Bets "Higher For Longer"; East Bay Board Eases To 2,915 Active On A 280-New Monday
real_estate.commentary:
The 30-year fixed is holding at 6.59% for a third straight day, with the 15-year at 6.09%. The bigger story is the one Wall Street is now saying out loud: Deutsche Bank just raised its year-end forecast for the 10-year Treasury to 4.70% and says the Fed, under new Chair Kevin Warsh, is done cutting (more in Economy). The buyer sitting on the sidelines waiting for a big rate drop may be playing a long game that does not pay off.

Local board: 2,915 active, down 49 from Friday, on 280 new listings and 212 closed sales. That is the Monday refresh with the weekend's new supply now posted, and it is the biggest one-day new count we have seen in weeks.

Two national notes worth passing along. First, "buy before you sell" is getting easier: firms like Flyhomes and HomeLight will now buy your current home so you can qualify for the next loan without carrying two payments, which matters when roughly 60% of sellers are buyers too. Second, the grind is real, with four years of high rates thinning the agent ranks. NAR membership is down to 1.4 million from 1.6 million in 2022 and the sales pace is the slowest since 1982. The agents still standing are the ones who adapted.

For agents: inventory is building at the top of the week while rates look stuck near 6.6% and the smart money bets they stay there. Do not sell buyers on a rate cut that may not come, sell them on the home and price it to today's market.
